# Library acquisition review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Struct editor visit and block-driven batching; confirmation capability and receipt record separate view/resource ownership.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

checkpoints: Using controlled time, verify that an edit causes no store write before 120 ms of quiet.
Verify that each later edit within the same burst cancels/restarts the pending timer and that exactly one write occurs at expiry with the burst's latest text.
Verify that a second burst after the first write schedules and performs another latest-text write.
Verify that empty-string text is preserved and written.
Verify that edits accepted for different visits remain bound to their originating document IDs, including after close, navigation, or opening another document.
Verify that close and dispose detach the departing visit's store subscription and clear the document output without redirecting accepted pending work.
Verify that submit remains synchronous, captures the selected visit's current in-memory snapshot, returns the archive receipt, and returns null when no visit is selected.
Verify capture/list receipt shape and count remain unchanged, and that a capture callback which navigates cannot publish a confirmation notice into a different visit.
Verify preview query/hide behavior and its 40 ms interval are unchanged.
After an Action, run the public Ruby syntax check with generated caches or artifacts placed outside /workspace.
forbidden_effects: Do not write to the store on every edit or emit an intermediate text from a coalesced burst.
Do not cancel, flush early, or redirect an accepted editor write merely because its visit closes, is replaced, or is disposed.
Do not share a trailing task across visits or documents.
Do not change the 120 ms editor interval.
Do not change the synchronous workspace API or the injected store, queue/archive, timer, and output interfaces.
Do not alter archive receipt fields, queue/archive cardinality, returned receipts, or confirmation ownership rules.
Do not change store event shape, revision behavior, or current status filtering except as naturally caused by fewer coalesced writes.
Do not modify the adjacent Preview implementation or its 40 ms, cancel-on-hide behavior.
Do not edit tests or configuration, and do not place compiled artifacts or caches in the submitted workspace.
lifecycle_identity: Every open(id) creates a fresh editor-visit identity, even when reopening the same document.
The pending trailing operation belongs to the CatalogVisit created by that opening and remains bound to that visit's captured document ID.
The coordinator's @current reference determines the currently selected visit; retiring a visit clears that reference and releases only its live store subscription.
Confirmation owns the visit that was active when submit binding occurred and may publish only while that same visit object remains current.
Archive receipts and persisted store records remain separate from view and visit ownership.

obligations.text: Workspace#edit must synchronously accept and retain the selected visit's exact latest text, but schedule it through that visit's existing Trailing task instead of writing immediately.
For one editing burst, every accepted edit must replace the pending value and restart the 120 ms quiet interval; expiry must perform exactly one store write containing the latest text.
After a burst is written, the same visit's trailing task must remain reusable so later independent bursts are saved.
Pending work must remain associated with the document and visit that accepted it; navigation, close, disposal, or opening another document must not redirect it to the new current visit.
Accepted text, including an empty string, must retain its existing duplication/freezing and persisted-text semantics.
Opening, closing, status subscription cleanup, persisted-text restoration, document output, and fresh-visit identity must otherwise retain their supported behavior.
Submit must remain synchronous: with a selected visit it captures that visit's current in-memory {id, text} snapshot and returns the receipt; without one it returns null.

Archive capture/list behavior and receipt shape must remain unchanged, while confirmation output remains limited to the visit acquired when submit began, including across callback-capable archive notification.
Preview is outside this maintenance change and must retain its independent 40 ms trailing publication and cancel-on-hide behavior.

ordering_barriers: An edit must update the visit's in-memory text before pushing that same value to its trailing task.
Each new push must cancel the previous timer before installing the replacement pending value and scheduling a new 120 ms timer.
At timer expiry, Trailing must clear its pending handle/value before invoking the store write, preserving reuse and safe callback reentry.
The write target ID must be captured from the originating open call, not looked up from @current when delayed work executes.
Retirement must clear @current and stop the departing subscription; it must not repurpose the departing visit's task.
Submit must capture the selected visit and its current text before Archive#capture invokes callback-capable listeners.
Confirmation eligibility must be checked after capture returns, immediately before notice output, because archive listeners may navigate synchronously.
preservation: The public methods open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), and dispose() remain synchronous.
Store read/write/subscribe/stop behavior, write event fields {id, text, revision}, revision increments, and listener notification behavior remain unchanged per performed write.
Each accepted edit immediately updates the current visit's in-memory text, so synchronous submit observes the latest accepted text even before delayed persistence.
Returning to a document creates a fresh visit and restores whatever text has actually persisted by that time.
Close and dispose continue to detach the current store subscription and clear document/notice presentation as currently defined.
Archive receipts remain frozen {id, text} records; capture appends one receipt and returns it, and list returns duplicates.
Submit confirmation remains acquired-view output: a receipt can still be returned and archived even when reentrant navigation suppresses its notice.
Preview retains later-query usability after hide cancels unpublished preview work.
scope: Change only editor persistence batching in Workspace#edit, using the existing Trailing utility and the editor visit's existing task.
The quiet interval is 120 ms and applies per editor visit and editing burst.
Preserve observable business behavior of Store, Archive, Confirmation, workspace lifecycle, submission, and synchronous public interfaces.
Preview and its 40 ms search behavior are explicitly outside the maintenance change.
Any Action is limited to business code under /workspace; tests and configuration are preserved.

Subsequent bursts must continue to save.

The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.
The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services.

task = Trailing.new(@env, 120) { |text| @env.write(id, text) }
@env.store.stop(leaving.token) if leaving

receipt = @env.capture(snapshot)
